memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Anything she lies on during her period will be unclean, and anything she sits on will be unclean. Anyone who touches her bed will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Her bed. Her seat. And everyone who touches them.

This was ordinary life for half of Israel. Every month, a woman's presence reshaped the household — where she sat, what she handled, who could touch her. She did not choose it and could not avoid it.

There is a lesson here about burdens people carry without choosing them. Some difficulties in life are chosen, and some are simply given. Chronic pain. A family situation. A responsibility that landed on you because there was no one else. A body that limits what you can do.

The world often assumes people are responsible for their own hardships. Job's friends assumed it. The disciples assumed it when they asked whose sin caused a man's blindness (John 9:2). We assume it too, more often than we admit.

But God knows the difference between what we have chosen and what has been laid on us. He deals with us accordingly. As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him; for he knows how we are formed, he remembers that we are dust (Ps 103:13-14).

If you are carrying something you never chose, God is not standing over you asking why you have not fixed it. He is close.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What burden are you carrying that you never chose?
2. Do you assume God blames you for it?
3. Who around you is carrying an unchosen weight that you could help lift?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know what I have chosen and what has simply been laid on me. Thank You for Your compassion. Help me carry what I must and to help others carry theirs. Amen.
